title: shark pop-up card
what you'll need: Cardstock, scissors, markers
instructions:
The Base Fold: Fold a piece of cardstock in half to create your card. Keep it folded.

The Mouth Cut: On the folded edge, use scissors to make one straight cut (about 2 inches long) directly into the center of the card.

The Triangle Folds: Take the two corners created by that cut and fold them back away from the center to create two small triangles. Crease these triangles very firmly with your fingernail.

The Reverse Crease: Unfold the two small triangles so the card is flat (but still folded in half).

The Pop: Open the card slightly. Use your finger to push the two triangle "flaps" through to the inside of the card.

The Set: Close the card flat and press down hard. When you open the card now, the triangles should pop inward, creating a "beak" or "mouth" that opens and closes.
variations: different animals

title: pop up farm
what you'll need: Cardstock, markers, scissors, glue
instructions:
The Backdrop: Fold a large piece of blue cardstock in half to create the background sky and the base of your card.

The Fan Floor: Take a rectangular piece of orange paper and fold it back and forth in even "mountain and valley" folds to create a long accordion fan.

The Center Anchor: Fold your finished accordion fan in half to find the center point.

Gluing the Fan: Apply glue to the two flat outer ends of the fan.

The Pop-Up Mechanism: Press the center fold of the fan into the center crease of your blue card.

Securing the Fan: Glue the left edge of the fan to the left side of the card and the right edge to the right side of the card, making sure the fan sits flat against the bottom edge.

Decoration: Once the glue is dry, open the card to watch the fan spread out into a semi-circle "floor."

Finishing Touches: Glue your house and character cut-outs to the blue background and tuck small grass cut-outs into the folds of the orange fan.

title: Self-Watering Terrarium! : 7 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description: Self-Watering Terrarium!: Don't have 4.5 billion years to make a planet? Make your own tiny world on the quick and cheap! After you throw in the basics, cap it off with an ozone, and let life take over. This terrarium is a great quick project to introduce kiddos (and adults,…
what you'll need:
Recycled tennis ball container with cap (we ask at tennis courts, but other plastic containers will do)
Sand
Potting soil
Water
Seeds (scarlet runner beans and grass seeds are excellent)
Small cup for pouring
instructions:
add sand  (two finger widths deep),  4 fingers of soil (DO NOT MIX LAYERS), For the big seeds, make a hole with your finger or a pencil, drop it in, and cover it up. A general rule is to bury seeds at a depth approximately half their longest dimension. You can place a second big seed in there, in case the first one doesn't germinate, but make sure to spread them apart. Don't want them competing too much!

For small seeds, you can just sprinkle them on top. For grass, it grows everywhere (that's what it's bred for!), so you can go heavy with this and they're pretty much guaranteed to grow.                                          To begin the self-watering cycle, we're going to add some in slowly. Grab a small cup, and water your terrarium slowly. You can even tilt and pour down the side of the container to minimize impact with the soil. As you pour, if you look down the side, you can see water seeping down to the sand layer. You want to keep pouring until your soil looks like a nice, chocolate cake mix but without pools.

What's exciting is that after you add this water, you never have to water again. That's right, all the water that ends up in our plants is from that initial bit that you added.                                                                if you add too much water try adding more dry soil on top to absorb the extra water, but it will make it harder for your seeds to grow.                                                                                                                                                                                         put the lid on and leave it on (whatever you end up using must be properly sealed or the water will escape)  LEAVE IN A SUNNY SPOT

title: salt volcano
what you'll need: Salt, food coloring, water, oil, jar, spoon
instructions:
1. Add the Water
Pour 1 cup of water into your clear jar or glass. This is the base layer of your volcano.
2. Add Food Coloring (Optional)
Want a fiery eruption or an underwater lava flow? Add 2–3 drops of food coloring and stir gently. 3. Pour in the Oil
Slowly pour ¼ cup of vegetable oil into the jar. The oil will float on top of the water—don’t mix them!
4. Sprinkle in the Salt
Now comes the fun! Gently sprinkle a spoonful of salt on top of the oil. Watch as it sinks, pulling blobs of oil down and creating bubbly, erupting effects as it rises again. 5. Repeat and Enjoy
Keep adding salt in small amounts to continue the eruptions. Try different types or amounts to change the effect!

title: invisible ink
what you'll need:
water (1/2 cup)
baking soda (1 Tablespoon)
paper
q-tips (or a paintbrush) to apply invisible ink
rubbing alcohol (1/2 cup)
turmeric (1 teaspoon)
paper towels (or a paintbrush) to apply color-changing solution
instructions:
1. First, add 1 Tablespoon of baking soda to 1/2 cup of water.

2. Stir the baking soda into the water to make the “invisible ink”.

3. Use q-tips (or paintbrushes) to draw a picture with the invisible ink on paper.

4. While you are waiting for your paper to dry, mix up your color changing-solution. First, add 1 teaspoon of turmeric to 1/2 cup of rubbing alcohol.

5. Stir the turmeric into the rubbing alcohol. (Note: The solution can stain a little bit. I used a white plastic bowl, which was not the smartest, because it was a little difficult to clean afterwards. You might want to use a glass bowl.)

6. After the paper is dry, use a paper towel (or paintbrush) to apply the color-changing solution to the paper to reveal the secret message! (Note: We used paper towels, but our hands were all a little orange for a few hours afterward, so you might want to use a paintbrush instead!)

instructions: sort items into cold and hot piles, see what their reasoning is

title: Materials game:
description: write a material on a sticky pad and ask the kids to stick it on something made of that material. Or if outside say to go touch something, inside ask them to bring something made of that material
what you'll need: Sticky notes, markers
instructions: 1. Write a material name (e.g., "Wood," "Plastic," "Metal") on a sticky note. 2. Have the child go around the house and stick the note on something made of that material. 3. If outside, play a "Touch Game"—say "Go touch something made of stone!" 4. Discuss how each material feels (cold, hard, smooth). 5. This builds an early understanding of material properties.

title: vehicle place
what you'll need: Play mat with roads/water/sky, toy vehicles
instructions: 1. Provide a mat or drawing showing land, sea, and air. 2. Give the child a variety of toy vehicles (boat, car, plane). 3. Have the child "place" each vehicle in its correct environment. 4. Discuss why a bus stays on the road and a boat stays in the water. 5. Roleplay a long journey using all three types of transport.

title: Preschool Art Lesson: Kandinsky's Circles : 6 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description: Preschool Art Lesson: Kandinsky's Circles: Your child can make an easy, colorful, and fun painting inspired by Wassily Kandinsky's well-known painting Color Study: Squares with Concentric Circles. This project is best suited for ages 3 through 5. Children may need help with measuring or fold…
what you'll need: Paper divided into squares, oil pastels
instructions: 1. In each square, draw a small circle in the center. 2. Draw larger concentric circles around it in different colors. 3. Fill the whole grid with colorful circles like Kandinsky.

title: lolly stick colour match dominos
what you'll need: Lolly sticks, markers
instructions: 1. Paint the ends of lolly sticks in different colors (e.g., half red, half blue). 2. Take turns placing a stick down, but only if the color matches the end of the previous stick. 3. This is a simplified version of dominos. 4. See how long of a "train" you can build. 5. Discuss the strategy of saving certain colors for later.

title: buttoncolours
what you'll need: differnt coloured buttons, different coloured fabrics
instructions: sew buttons onto piece of fabric, cut out other pieces of fabric that match the colours of the buttons, see how quickly they can identify the matching pairs and button them on.

title: colourfeeders
what you'll need: Colored cardboard tubes, matching colored pom-poms
instructions: 1. Decorate cardboard tubes as "monsters" or "animals" of different colors. 2. Cut a "mouth" in each tube. 3. Have the child use a spoon or tweezers to "feed" the matching colored pom-poms to each animal. 4. Count how many pom-poms each animal ate. 5. Discuss which color was the most popular.
variations: print out coloured characters and coloured foods, discuss which foods are which colours and the childs preferences.

title: jarcolourmatch
what you'll need: Glass jars, colored water, matching lids or items
instructions: 1. Fill jars with water dyed different colors. 2. Provide a bin of small items (beads, buttons) that match those colors. 3. Have the child drop the matching items into the correct colored jar. 4. Discuss how the items look under the water. 5. This is a calm, focused sensory activity.
variations: see how different coloured items look in different coloured water

title: tape colour match
what you'll need: Different colors of tape, matching colored toys
instructions: 1. Place strips of different colored tape on a table or floor. 2. Have the child find objects in the house that match each tape color. 3. Place the objects on the corresponding tape line. 4. Count how many items were found for each color. 5. Discuss which color was the easiest to find.

title: sticky note rainbow hunt
description: make a line of 1 each of different coloured sticky notes somewhere and hide 4 more of each colour on something around the house, once they have found one they put it under the one in the row
what you'll need: Multi-colored sticky notes
instructions: 1. Place one "base" sticky note of each color in a row on a wall. 2. Hide 4-5 matching sticky notes of each color around the room. 3. The child must find a hidden note and "match" it by placing it underneath the base note. 4. Continue until all columns are filled. 5. Time the activity to add a challenge.

title: colour smashing under clingfilm
what you'll need: Paper, liquid paint, clingfilm (plastic wrap)
instructions: 1. Place several drops of different colored paint on a piece of paper. 2. Carefully cover the entire paper with a layer of clingfilm. 3. Have the child "smash" and spread the paint through the plastic with their fingers. 4. Observe the colors blending without getting hands messy. 5. Peel back the film to see the final textured masterpiece.
variations: after it's dry add black paper cutouts as shadows if you want. the art created in the activity could also be used as a reverse colouring book.

title: Color Photo Breakdown and Build Up - Exploring the REAL Primary Colors : 6 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description: Color Photo Breakdown and Build Up - Exploring the REAL Primary Colors: Have you ever wondered how the colored inks in your printer work together to create a full color photograph? Follow along as we show you how to decompose a full color photograph into the primary colors of ink and then recompose the full color image …
what you'll need: computer,printer, transparency paper
instructions: print pictures split into cyan, magenta and blue, onto transparency paper, cut them out and experiment with overlaying them with each other

title: coloursampleart
what you'll need: Paint sample cards (from hardware store), glue, paper
instructions: 1. Collect a variety of paint sample cards in different hues. 2. Cut the cards into shapes or strips. 3. Glue the pieces onto paper to create a "gradient" artwork or a mosaic. 4. Arrange colors from lightest to darkest. 5. Discuss the names of the different colors (e.g., "Sky Blue" vs "Navy").
variations: you don't have to glue down the pieces, it can be reusable temporary art

title: runaround game show quiz
what you'll need: Runaround Game Show format
instructions: ask a multiple choice question, the children have 15 seconds to run to a designated spot that represents one of the answers, the question is repeated and they have another 15 seconds if they want to change their minds, the answer is revealed
variations: do after learning something or reading a book to see what they've retained, it's a good way to get  a movement break in

title: karaoke
description: find karaoke versions of your childs favurite songs on youtube
what you'll need: YouTube Karaoke videos
instructions: 1. Find the "karaoke" or "instrumental with lyrics" version of a favorite song. 2. Use a hairbrush as a microphone. 3. Sing along to the music. 4. This builds confidence in performance and helps with word recognition. 5. Discuss the "story" being told in the song.

title: talking pirates
what you'll need: paper, pens, pegs
instructions: draw a pirate, cut off the head from the top lip, glue this part to the top side of a peg and the rest to the bottom, pinch the pegs to  open the mouth and release to close
variations: do with any kind of character you want

title: Kinderkid Pride : 3 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description:
Kinderkid Pride: While celebrating PRIDE month my 4/5-year-olds had the opportunity to paint their favorite thing....A RAINBOW.
After painting the basic rainbow we added a little extra detail in each section with another shade or tint of the first color used. The ch…
what you'll need: Paper, rainbows, symbols of kindness/pride
instructions: paint a rainbow and fill in each colour with a different kind of pattern
variations: draw something that is that colour in its area e.g. a sun in yellow or a different fruit for each colour

title: sussex wildlife trust events
what you'll need: Sussex Wildlife Trust website
instructions: 1. Check the website for local nature events, workshops, and guided walks. 2. Plan a visit to a nearby reserve based on their suggestions. 3. Participate in a "Wild Beach" or "Forest School" session if available. 4. Use their seasonal guides to know what to look for in nature this month. 5. This connects your family to local conservation efforts.

title: who's in the window?
what you'll need: paper cups, scissors, pens
instructions: cut a window out of a paper cup and decorate the cup like a house, get another paper cup and put it inside the first one, use the window as a stencil and draw it on the inner cup, turn the inner cup so the next window can follow on directly from that one, do windows until you run out of space, draw whatever characters you want in the windows and turn the cup to see the others
variations: could be used for storytelling when something happens in a certain order e.g. gruffalo characters

title: tortoise and hare racers
what you'll need: Paper, markers, string, straws, glue or tape
instructions: draw a tortoise and hare, stick 2 pieces of a straw to each in a v shape (but leave a gap between the closer ends), thread a piece of string through one of the pieces of the straw (towards the pointed end) and back through the other piece of straw (from the pointed end), have a child hold the 2 ends of the string and bring the character all the way to their hands, take the loop of string and put it around a doorknob, have the child pull the string outwards to make the character move up the string. If you have multiple children they can race each other.
variations: could be any characters or animals  or vehicles you want

title: big beaks
what you'll need: 2 sheets of A3 paper, glue, scissors, string or elastic
instructions: follow folding instructions on picture, poke holes for string or elastic to put around ears

title: egg box crocodile
what you'll need: egg cartons, green paint, string, scissors
instructions: cut all the long pointy bits of hte egg carton out  and poke a small hole in the top of each one, connect 2 facing opposite directions with string and stack the rest following the direction of the first one on that side. tie string at ends to hold it all together and add feet.
variations: for a snake just do them all going in the same direction and leave more slack if you want it to be more wiggly.

title: paper plate chickens
what you'll need: Paper plate, yellow paint, feathers, paper
instructions: 1. Paint a paper plate yellow and fold it in half. 2. Glue googly eyes and a paper beak to the front. 3. Glue yellow feathers to the back for a tail. 4. Add orange paper "feet" at the bottom.

title: egg box turtle
what you'll need: Egg carton, green paint, markers, scissors
instructions: cut out turtle shape as shown in picture

title: egg box toadstools
what you'll need: Egg carton, red and white paint
instructions: 1. Cut individual cups out of an egg carton. 2. Paint the cups bright red. 3. Once dry, add white "polka dots" with a cotton swab. 4. put small rount bits on tall pointy bits
variations: could make a game of trying to toss the "hat" on the base

title: Cardboard and Velcro Building Tiles : 7 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description: Cardboard and Velcro Building Tiles: These cardboard Velcero Building Tiles are wonderful for so many reasons. Unlike Magna-Tiles, they don't come crashing down as easily and loudly, which is great news for my classroom. Also because they are held together with Velcro, you can create a…
what you'll need: Cardboard shapes, Velcro dots
instructions: 1. Cut cardboard into squares and triangles. 2. Apply "hook" dots to one side and "loop" dots to the other. 3. Connect the tiles together to build 3D geometric structures.
variations: could try different types of fasteners e.g. popper buttons or magnets

title: dino headdress
what you'll need: Cardboard, green paint, elastic
instructions: 1. Cut several large triangles out of cardboard. 2. Paint them green. 3. Tape the triangles to a strip of cardboard that fits around the head. 4. Ensure the "spikes" stand up straight. 5. Wear the headdress and stomp around like a dinosaur.

title: toilet roll racecar
what you'll need: Toilet paper roll, 4 bottle caps, straws, skewers
instructions: 1. Paint a toilet paper roll your favorite racing color. 2. Poke two holes through the sides of the roll at the front and back. 3. Slide straws through the holes, then skewers through the straws. 4. Attach bottle caps to the ends of the skewers as wheels. 5. Cut a small "U" shape in the top for a cockpit and add a paper driver.

title: egg box teddy bears
what you'll need: Egg carton, paint/pens
instructions: cut out bear shape as shown in picture

title: paper plate seagulls
what you'll need: Paper plate, blue/gray paint, yellow paper
instructions: cut body shape out of centre of plate, use the other 2 sides as wings, decorate and position
variations: use split pins or string/treasury tags to make flappable wings

title: building foam
what you'll need: Shaving cream, glue, cardstock
instructions: 1. Mix shaving cream and glue to create "foam." 2. Use the foam to build 3D structures on cardstock. 3. Once dry, the foam remains "puffy" and soft. 4. Add food coloring to create colorful "buildings." 5. This is a great sensory-heavy construction project.

title: construction foam
what you'll need: shaving cream, sand
instructions: mix them together and use as mortar for play bricks

title: paper cup shark snacker
what you'll need: Paper cups, scissors, pens
instructions: cut a window out of a paper cup and draw a sharks open mouth around it, get another paper cup and put it inside the first one, use the window as a stencil and draw it on the inner cup, turn the inner cup so the next window can follow on directly from that one, do windows until you run out of space, draw whatever the shark will eat in the windows and turn the cup to see the others

title: pen push
tags: fine motor, pen grip, mark making
skills: Coordination, Force, fine motor, pen grip, mark making
what you'll need: paper, pens/pencils, any small item
instructions: put a small object on a piece of paper and get the child to try to move it around using their pen/pencil, you could give them a goal to get to or you could do it with little cars and draw parking spots to get to

title: walking feet
what you'll need: Paper, scissors, tape, straws or skewers
instructions: cut 2 feet shapes out of paper, attach each to a bit of straw or skewer and stick on opposite sides of the inside of a roll of tape

title: walk the plank
what you'll need: Long wooden plank or tape on the floor
instructions: 1. Place a plank on the ground (or use tape to mark a line). 2. Imagine you are on a pirate ship. 3. Walk from one end to the other without stepping off the "plank."

title: treasure bridge
what you'll need: Tape on floor, "treasures" (blocks)
instructions: 1. Place two lines of tape on the floor as a "bridge." 2. Scatter "treasures" along the bridge. 3. The child must walk the bridge and pick up the treasures without falling off. 4. Increase the difficulty by making the bridge narrower. 5. See how many treasures they can carry at once.

title: bridge balance
what you'll need: tape, block (or car for added difficulty), 2 things the same height to build tape bridge across (like tables or chairs), pen/pencil/stick
instructions: make a bridge with the tape (sticky side down) and see if your child can push a block all the way across without it falling off (try with finger first and then move on to pushing with a different item like a pen)
